headline: Margins snap back and full-year guidance moves higher
summary_short: Hershey reported Q2 FY2026 net sales of $2.787 billion (+6.6% y/y) with reported diluted EPS of $2.26 versus $0.31 a year ago, while adjusted diluted EPS rose 57% to $1.90; the company raised its full-year 2026 sales and earnings outlook.
summary_long: Net sales rose 6.6% y/y to $2.787B; organic constant-currency growth was 3.6% on ~12 points of pricing against an ~8-point volume decline, partly offset by the LesserEvil acquisition. Reported gross margin jumped to 45.3% (from 30.5%) mainly on a $102.9M favorable derivative mark-to-market swing versus a $200.7M loss last year; adjusted gross margin rose 350bp to 41.6% on pricing, lower commodity costs, and productivity savings. Reported EPS of $2.26 and net income of $457.7M reflect that easy comparison; adjusted diluted EPS of $1.90 rose 57%. Cash fell to $791.2M from $912.3M a year ago. Hershey raised full-year 2026 guidance: net sales growth to 4.5%-5%, organic growth to 3%-3.5%, reported EPS growth to 82%-89%, and adjusted EPS growth to 32.5%-35%.

drivers.explanation: Organic constant-currency growth of 3.6% was driven by ~12 points of net price realization, partly offset by ~8 points of volume decline from elasticity in Confectionery and International; the LesserEvil acquisition added 2.7 points.

Reported gross margin expansion was driven by net price realization, a favorable derivative mark-to-market swing, lower net commodity costs, and productivity savings, partly offset by higher logistics expenses and unfavorable mix.
Reported net income growth mainly reflects a swing from a $200.7M commodity-derivative mark-to-market loss a year ago to a $102.9M gain this quarter, on top of core pricing and cost gains.
Full-year 2026 outlook was raised across net sales growth, organic growth, reported EPS growth, and adjusted EPS growth, citing a strong first half and momentum into the second half.
